🇧🇪

Belgium

27 ads · €4620 spend · 172 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Carousel format is the undisputed king — "Carousel_120237873305580396 - Copy" leads with €960 spend, 50 purchases, and a 9.16x ROAS at €19.2 CPP. Scalable and proven.
• WCDxBA concept is the most consistent winner across variants — #5 (10.3x ROAS), #1 (5.11x ROAS), and #2 (3.45x ROAS) all deliver. Strong collab/concept angle resonates in Belgium.
• Product-hero statics crush it at low CPP — "Static _ Diamond Earstud #4" delivers a 10.04x ROAS at an absurd €9.47 CPP on only €47 spend. Starved of budget.
❌ What's Not Working
• "Video _ Creative #3" is a money pit — €127 spent, 1 purchase, 0.59x ROAS, €126.54 CPP. High CTR but zero conversion. The creative attracts clicks but repels buyers.
• Partner concept is bloated and inconsistent — "Static _ Partner #2" ate €310 for only 6 purchases at €51.68 CPP (2.48x ROAS), while #4 spent €44 with zero purchases. The angle isn't landing at scale.
• "Static _ Heart Tag #1" spent €80 with zero purchases despite 174% CTR — pure click bait with no conversion path. Meanwhile UGC statics (#2 at €59.62 CPP) are underperforming their format potential.
⬆ Double Down On
• Carousel formats immediately — only one carousel is running and it's the top performer. Create carousel variants for WCDxBA, Diamond Earstud, and Summer concepts.
• Product-focused statics with single hero items — Diamond Earstud #4 and WCDxBA #5 prove that clean, product-forward statics convert at 10x+ ROAS. Produce more variants across jewelry categories (rings, necklaces, ear studs).
• WCDxBA collab/concept angle across all formats — this concept works in 4 out of 5 variants. Expand it into carousel and video to compound the win.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Pause "Video _ Creative #3" now — 0.59x ROAS is actively destroying margin. No iteration will save this creative.
• Pause "Static _ Heart Tag #1" — €80, zero purchases. The variant #2 works; this one doesn't. Stop bleeding.
• Stop scaling the Partner concept until you fix the landing experience — €475 total spend across 4 variants with inconsistent results and the worst average CPP in the account.

🇩🇪

Germany

3 ads · €910 spend · 7 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Video _ Kay #1 is the only ad approaching viable efficiency — ROAS 1.82x at €72 CPP on just €216 spend, suggesting the Kay concept resonates with DE audiences.
• Video format is driving all 7 purchases in this market; both video ads converted while the static generated zero.
• High CTR across all three ads indicates the brand aesthetic and creative hooks are attracting clicks — the funnel breaks post-click, not pre-click.
❌ What's Not Working
• Video _ Stack #1 absorbed 68% of total spend (€589) yet delivered only 1.11x ROAS at a brutal €147 CPP — this ad is actively destroying margin.
• Static _ Earstud New #1 has the highest CTR but zero purchases from €106 spend — classic vanity-metric trap; clicks without conversion intent.
• Germany is being tested with only 3 creatives total, zero UGC, and zero German-language-specific concepts — the market is starved of creative diversity.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more Kay-style creative — this concept converts at 2x the efficiency of Stack; extend it into UGC and static variants before scaling spend.
• Lean into video-first strategy for DE; both converting ads are video while the only static flopped — this market clearly responds to motion and storytelling.
• Create DE-specific hooks and copy: affordable luxury messaging may need cultural adaptation (price transparency, quality craftsmanship from Antwerp) to convert German shoppers who index high on value justification.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop feeding Video _ Stack #1 — €589 at 1.11x ROAS is subsidizing Meta, not growing the brand.
• Kill Static _ Earstud New #1 immediately — high CTR with zero purchases means curiosity clickers, not buyers.
• Stop running only 3 ads in an entire country market — this is not enough creative volume to learn or win.

Kamping Kitsch Club — Ads Report

Meta Ads + Google Ads · Creative insights + Performance

AI

Creative Analysis

30 ads · Meta · last 30 days

Split by country · Click any card → public post · Green border = ROAS ≥3 · Yellow = ROAS ≥1.5 · Red = no purch.

🇧🇪

Belgium

30 ads · €3329 spend · 478 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Price-math and discount-code statics are the real heroes — "Static _ Berekening #2" hits 36.69x ROAS at €2.86 CPP, "Static _ Code #1" hits 30.6x ROAS. Value-framing converts.
• Emotional urgency statics scale profitably — "Static _ Hart #2" drove 113 purchases at 17.31x ROAS, "Static _ Update #1" added 89 more at 18.19x. These are the volume engines.
• Static format dominates everything. 18 of 20 ads are static, carrying 99%+ of all conversions. This is a static-first account despite the brand's video-first identity.
❌ What's Not Working
• Video is a money pit for conversion campaigns — "Video _ Aftermovie #1" burned €144 for 4 purchases (CPP €36.08), "Video _ McDrummer Vrijgezelle" spent €24 for zero purchases. Combined ROAS ~1.5x.
• "Static _ Organic #1" is a clickbait trap — 1257% CTR but ROAS 0.94x. Attracts curiosity clickers, not ticket buyers. Spending at a loss.
• Review creative is wildly inconsistent — "Static _ Review #2" spent €31 for 1 purchase while "Static _ Review #3" got 10 purchases from €27. Format isn't the issue, the specific creative is.
⬆ Double Down On
• More Berekening-style price-math statics — cost per hour, cost vs a night out, cost split between friends. This angle has the best ROAS in the entire account and is barely spending.
• Scale the Code/discount mechanic aggressively — both Code #1 variants crush (19-30x ROAS). Create flash codes, early-bird codes, group codes. Urgency + savings = conversions.
• Expand the Hart emotional series into new angles — Hart #2 is the proven volume king. Produce Hart #4, #5 with fresh emotional hooks tied to FOMO, nostalgia, and community.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop running aftermovies and artist teaser videos in conversion campaigns immediately. Both videos: €168 spent, 4 total purchases. Use video for top-of-funnel awareness only, never for purchase optimization.
• Kill "Static _ Organic #1" — losing money at 0.94x ROAS. A 1257% CTR that doesn't convert is worse than useless, it's training the algorithm on junk clickers.
• Pause "Static _ Review #2" — €31 for 1 purchase with no attributable ROAS. "Static _ Review #3" proves the format can work, so the creative itself is the problem.

AI

Creative Analysis

20 ads · Meta · last 30 days

Split by country · Click any card → public post · Green border = ROAS ≥3 · Yellow = ROAS ≥1.5 · Red = no purch.

🇧🇪

Belgium

20 ads · €829 spend · 45 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Urgency and countdown messaging dominates: "Video _ Urgency #3" (21 purch., 6.66x ROAS) and "Video _ Tickets Countdown #4" (14 purch., 25.43x ROAS at €2.76 CPP) are the clear engines.
• Scarcity framing converts at absurd efficiency — "Static _ Urgency #6" and "Static _ Paradisco Key Visual #1" both show 20x+ ROAS on tiny spend, signaling untapped scale potential in static formats.
• Video urgency creative carries the account: two ads account for 35 of 45 total purchases.
❌ What's Not Working
• Lineup-focused creative is a money pit: "Video _ Saturday Lineup #1" burned €244 for 1 purchase (0.21x ROAS) — the worst performer by far. "Video _ Friday Lineup #1" spent €25 with zero conversions.
• Aftermovie content doesn't convert: "Video _ Aftermovie #1" managed 1.5x ROAS at €34 CPP — brand content masquerading as performance ads.
• Meta is severely under-investing in the best creative: "Video _ Tickets Countdown #4" has 25.43x ROAS but only €39 spend — budget allocation is broken.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more urgency + countdown video variants — this angle owns 80% of conversions. Test different countdown hooks (final hours, last 50 tickets, price tier expiring).
• Scale static urgency formats aggressively — early signals from "Static _ Urgency #6" and "Static _ Paradisco Key Visual #1" suggest statics can convert cheaper than video with the right scarcity hook.
• Create hybrid creatives: combine aftermovie energy footage with urgency overlays and countdown text to merge emotion with conversion triggers.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all lineup reveal ads immediately — "Video _ Saturday Lineup #1" and "Video _ Friday Lineup #1" have collectively spent €269 for 1 purchase. Lineup info belongs on the landing page, not in paid creative.
• Stop running pure aftermovie content as conversion ads — "Video _ Aftermovie #1" and #2/#3 are awareness plays burning performance budget.
• Stop letting Meta allocate budget away from "Video _ Tickets Countdown #4" — force spend into this ad or its variants before the event sells out.

Belgium

13 ads · €4135 spend · 67 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Static offer creatives dominate: 'Static _ Offer #1 - Copy' is the clear winner at 7.35x ROAS and €47.94 CPP on the highest spend — proof the offer-led static format converts.
• Lifestyle statics punch above their weight: 'Static _ Lifestyle #2 - Copy' delivers the lowest CPP (€34.67) and near-scale ROAS (3.69x) on just €104 — massively underspent.
• Product-focused statics convert efficiently: 'Static _ Product Ziris #2' at 2.94x ROAS and €50.79 CPP shows product hero shots work for mid-funnel.
❌ What's Not Working
• Video underperforms statics across the board: 'Video _ Renée #1 - Copy' burned €741 at 1.23x ROAS (€92.58 CPP) — highest CPP in the account. Videos generate engagement but bleed money on conversion.
• The original 'Static _ Offer #1' at €976 spend delivers only 1.61x ROAS while its Copy variant hits 7.35x — identical creative likely trapped in a worse audience or placement; pure budget leak.
• Sieben Split videos ('Split #1' and 'Split #2') have zero purchases combined on €44 spend with below-average CTRs — no early signal of life.
⬆ Double Down On
• More static offer variants: the offer format is your proven converter. Create fresh angles on the same structure — new colorways, seasonal hooks, bundle offers, prescription upsell.
• Scale lifestyle statics aggressively: 'Static _ Lifestyle #2 - Copy' has the best CPP in the account at €34.67 and barely any spend. Produce more aspirational in-use imagery across cycling, running, and ski.
• Product hero statics per model: 'Static _ Product Ziris #2' proves product-first creative converts. Replicate for Helbo, Selva Snow, and photochromic/polarized lens variants.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Pause 'Video _ Renée #1 - Copy' immediately — €741 at 1.23x ROAS is the worst return-on-spend ratio in the account. That €741 belongs in 'Static _ Offer #1 - Copy'.
• Pause 'Static _ Offer #1' (original) — its Copy variant outperforms it by 4.5x on ROAS. Stop funding the loser twin.
• Cut 'Static _ Offer #4' — worst CTR in the account (52.74%), zero purchases. Dead on arrival.

🇳🇱

Netherlands

4 ads · €347 spend · 3 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Static _ Offer #3 shows the best efficiency at €55.81 CPP and 1.85x ROAS — only ad approaching viability in NL.
• Offer-based static creatives generate abnormally high click engagement across the board (100%+ CTR metrics), meaning the hook/visual grabs attention.
• NL market is responding to discount/offer framing — all 3 purchases came from offer-led creatives.
❌ What's Not Working
• Static _ Offer #1 ate 71% of total budget (€247) but returned only 1.29x ROAS — the campaign's biggest money drain with €123.60 CPP.
• Zero creative diversity: 4 static offer ads, no video, no UGC, no product education, no sport-specific angles. You're testing offer variants, not creative strategy.
• Massive click-to-purchase drop-off everywhere — sky-high engagement but almost no conversions suggests the landing page or post-click experience is broken for Dutch visitors.
⬆ Double Down On
• Offer #3's formula at lower CPP: lean into that specific offer framing/visual and iterate 3-4 variants around it before scaling.
• Product-specific creatives: Ziris for road/gravel cyclists, Helbo for enduro, Selva Snow for ski — NL has huge cycling and winter sports audiences you're not segmenting for.
• 'Op sterkte' sportbril angle: prescription sports glasses is the biggest differentiator vs Oakley/Decathlon and is completely absent from current creative.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop running Static _ Offer #1 — it's burning cash at 1.29x ROAS with enough spend to confirm it won't improve.
• Stop the all-static, all-offer creative strategy. Four near-identical ad formats teaches you nothing about what NL actually wants.
• Stop ignoring the post-click funnel — no amount of creative optimization fixes a leaky Dutch landing page.

Creative Analysis

7 ads · Meta · last 30 days

Split by country · Click any card → public post · Green border = ROAS ≥3 · Yellow = ROAS ≥1.5 · Red = no purch.

🇧🇪

Belgium

7 ads · €1690 spend · 124 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Catalog Carousel - Espresso Coffee is the runaway hero: 37.74x ROAS, 84 purchases, €12.29 CPP — dynamic product format + category segmentation is printing money.
• Retention audiences are gold: Static _ Hold #2 delivers the best CPP in the account (€7.18), Static _ Hold #1 runs at 19.96x ROAS, and Static _ Repeat #1 hits 29.51x ROAS on a tiny budget. Existing customers convert cheaply and repeatedly.
• Origin storytelling converts: Static _ Origin #1 at 9.33x ROAS proves that sourcing narratives resonate with this audience and drive real purchases, not just engagement.
❌ What's Not Working
• Static_Barista_Courses - Copy is an engagement trap: 77.53% CTR but only 1 purchase at €101.34 CPP. People click for the course content, not to buy beans. Wrong intent, wrong funnel stage.
• Prospecting is critically underfunded: Static _ Never #1 got only €14 in spend — impossible to learn or optimize cold acquisition with that budget. You're flying blind on top-of-funnel.
• No video creative in the mix at all. For a brand built on craft, origin stories, and barista culture, the absence of motion/UGC formats is a missed opportunity against scroll-stopping competition.
⬆ Double Down On
• Catalog carousels segmented by use case and category — replicate the Espresso carousel formula for filter, single origin, decaf, and subscription bundles.
• Retention static variants at volume — Hold #2's €7.18 CPP proves this audience converts dirt cheap; feed it 3-5 more creative variations to fight fatigue and scale spend.
• Origin and transparency storytelling for mid-funnel and prospecting — B-corp certification, farm-level sourcing, roast profiles. Static _ Origin #1 proves the angle works; now build it out across formats (video, carousel, UGC).
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop running Static_Barista_Courses as a purchase-optimized ad immediately. Either repurpose it for lead gen / email capture or kill it. A €101 CPP is unacceptable.
• Stop starving prospecting. Either commit real budget (€200+) to Static _ Never #1 or pull it — €14 teaches you nothing.
• Stop relying on statics only. Zero video or UGC in this account is a strategic gap that will cap your scale ceiling.

🇧🇪

Belgium

4 ads · €748 spend · 52 results
✅ What's Working
• "Static _ Investeren _ 2" is a machine — 52 leads at €13.38 CPL with sky-high CTR, proving the investment angle resonates hard with Belgian audiences.
• Static format clearly works for this audience — direct, clear investment messaging cuts through without needing video.
• The "Investeren" framing as primary hook validates that Belgian buyers treat Zeeland waterfront as a financial opportunity first, lifestyle second.
❌ What's Not Working
• "Static _ Investeren _ 3" burned €47 with zero conversions despite 130% CTR — people click but bounce, suggesting a creative-to-landing-page disconnect or weak post-click CTA.
• Zero creative diversity across the entire account — all static, all investment angle. No lifestyle, no kijkwoning, no second-home messaging. One ad carries 93% of spend.
• "Static _ Investeren _ 4" got algorithmically killed at €3 with 0% CTR — the creative is dead on arrival.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more investment-angle static variations — test different proof points (100% verhuurgarantie, fossil-free build quality, Westerschelde location premium) to find what specifically converts.
• Launch video creative showing the waterfront lifestyle — cinematic drone shots of the Westerschelde, the dike village, the space — to open a new emotional funnel that feeds the proven investment CTA.
• Create kijkwoning-specific ads with urgency and social proof — this is the bottom-funnel action the campaign exists for, yet no ad directly sells the visit.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill "Static _ Investeren _ 4" — zero CTR, algorithmically dead, not worth reviving.
• Stop running four near-identical static investment ads competing against each other — Meta's algorithm picked its winner in hours and starved the rest. Consolidate budget behind the winner and test genuinely different concepts instead.

Netherlands

6 ads · €1656 spend · 75 results
✅ What's Working
• "Static _ Water Wind _ Form" is the clear workhorse — €19.29 CPR at volume (59 results), proving lifestyle/emotional framing crushes rational investment messaging in this market.
• "Video _ Lifestyle #1" shows the highest CTR across all ads (447.72%) and a competitive €22.92 CPR on just €69 spend — video lifestyle content resonates hard with this audience.
• Dreamy, water-focused creative outperforms investment-angle statics by 40-60% on cost per result, confirming the target responds to aspiration over ROI logic.
❌ What's Not Working
• The four "Investeren" static variants are an over-indexed dead end — diminishing returns across the board, with CPR climbing from €31.86 to €44.65 as spend decreases. Investment-rational messaging is not the primary hook for this audience.
• "Static _ Investeren _ 4 - Copy" and "Static _ Investeren - Copy" collected €10 combined and zero results. Worst CTRs in the set (84.75% and 186.57%) — the creative is failing to stop the scroll.
• Heavy reliance on static formats when the one video ad outperforms every static on CTR by a wide margin. Only 1 of 6 ads is video — massive creative gap.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more video content in the lifestyle/cinematic lane — water, light, drone shots of the Westerschelde, slow-living moments. "Video _ Lifestyle #1" proves the format and angle work; now flood the algorithm with variants.
• Double down on the "Water Wind" emotional territory — nature, rust, ruimte, panoramic views. This is the proven conversion hook. Create 2-3 new statics and videos in this lane with varied hooks.
• Build kijkwoning-specific creative — the campaign goal is driving visits, but no ad explicitly sells the experience of visiting. Show the model home, create FOMO, give a reason to come this weekend.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop producing more "Investeren" static variants — four versions tested, all underperform the lifestyle angle. The investment message can live in copy, not as the creative lead.
• Kill "Static _ Investeren _ 4 - Copy" immediately — 84.75% CTR is abysmal and zero results. Dead creative.

Other

11 ads · €3762 spend · 330 results
✅ What's Working
• Visit-themed statics dominate efficiency — "Static _ Visit #2 - Copy" delivers 88 leads at €7.71 and "Static _ Nieuw_App #1" hits €7.42/lead, proving kijkwoning CTAs convert.
• "Static _ Water Wind _ Form" is the volume workhorse — 135 leads at €9.06 proves the dreamy water/wind lifestyle angle resonates at scale with Belgian/Dutch audiences.
• Original creatives consistently outperform copies — "Nieuw_App #1" (€7.42) vs Copy (€18.34), "Water Wind" (€9.06) vs Copy (€19.67). Duplication without iteration kills efficiency.
❌ What's Not Working
• "Static _ Review _ Form" is burning budget — €966 for just 34 leads at €28.41/result is 3x the cost of top performers. Social proof angle isn't landing in this format.
• Copy variants are dead weight — both "Water Wind _ Form - Copy" (€19.67) and "Nieuw_App #1 - Copy" (€18.34) are 2x+ worse than originals. Lazy duplication, no creative iteration.
• Video ads never got off the ground — "Video _ Testimonial #1" and "Video _ Lifestyle #1" have near-zero spend, suggesting Meta's algorithm instantly deprioritized them against stronger statics.
⬆ Double Down On
• Kijkwoning visit statics with direct CTAs — the Visit format is the cheapest lead driver. Produce new variants with seasonal hooks, interior shots, and urgency framing.
• Water/nature lifestyle statics — the Water Wind emotional angle proves aspirational waterfront imagery pulls leads. Expand with Westerschelde panoramic views, polder landscapes, golden hour shots.
• Apartment-specific statics — "Nieuw_App #1" at €7.42/lead proves product-specific messaging outperforms generic brand. Create equivalents for turnkey houses and hotel apartments with rental guarantee.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all Copy variants immediately — "Water Wind _ Form - Copy" and "Nieuw_App #1 - Copy" are cannibalizing budget from proven originals with zero creative differentiation.
• Pause "Static _ Review _ Form" — at €28.41/result it's the worst performer with meaningful spend. Reallocate its €966 monthly budget to top 3 performers.
• Stop duplicating ads without changing creative — every Copy underperforms. If testing, change hook, visual, or CTA, don't just clone.

Belgium

12 ads · €1719 spend · 309 results
✅ What's Working
• Sommerfeld creative direction delivers the cheapest leads: #2 at €3.09 and #3 at €4.91 across 94 combined results — clean modernist visuals clearly resonate with this audience.
• Bauhaus #5 is the undisputed volume workhorse — €602 spent, 101 results, €5.96 CPR — Meta's algorithm trusts it and keeps feeding it impressions.
• Static format overall is performing well for lead gen; sub-€6 CPR for high-end coastal real estate inquiries is exceptional value across the top 5 ads.
❌ What's Not Working
• Naoshima series is largely dead — #1 and #3 combined €8 spend, zero results. Even the one winner (#2 at €5.83) can't save a creative direction where 2 of 3 variants flopped.
• Bauhaus #4 is a clear outlier — €29.43 per result, 5× worse than the Bauhaus average. The algorithm deprioritized it for good reason.
• High-potential ads starved of budget: Bauhaus #1 (€3.23 CPR) and Sommerfeld #2 (€3.09 CPR) sit with tiny spend while less efficient variants eat the budget — likely an ad-set structure or DCO issue throttling winners.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more Sommerfeld-style creatives — this aesthetic direction has the best cost-efficiency at scale; iterate with new angles, crops, and copy overlays on that same visual language.
• Scale the hidden gems: Bauhaus #1 and Sommerfeld #2 have the lowest CPR in the entire account but are being budget-starved — isolate them or force spend allocation.
• Test video and carousel formats using the Sommerfeld and Bauhaus visual worlds — static is working, but you're leaving engagement and storytelling potential on the table for a product that demands walkthrough experiences.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill Naoshima #1 and #3 immediately — zero results, zero signal, wasting even tiny budget that could compound elsewhere.
• Kill Bauhaus #4 — €29 CPR with 1 result is not a data problem, it's a creative problem. Don't iterate, replace.
• Kill Bauhaus #3 — €11.77 CPR with only 1 result after meaningful impression delivery (361% CTR suggests clicks but no conversions). The landing page or creative promise is misaligned.

🇧🇪

Belgium

17 ads · €2503 spend · 103 results
✅ What's Working
• Specific use-case B2B angles dominate: "Açai Koffiebar" (34 results, €18.38), "4 Momenten #1" (24 results, €17.48), and "Upgrade Brunch" (16 results, €16.61) all convert because they speak to a concrete business scenario.
• Practical, operator-relevant framing (menu moments, brunch upgrades, coffee-bar context) drives 2–2.5× better CPR than generic benefit messaging.
• "Snel #2" hints at a speed/ease angle with the lowest CPR in the set (€12.78) — tiny sample but directionally strong.
❌ What's Not Working
• The "Boost" angle is broken: both variants (#1 at €40.22, #2 at €42.22) cost 2.5× more per result than top performers — vague benefit language doesn't resonate with B2B prospects.
• Consumer-facing statics are burning cash with zero conversions: "Nutri A #2" ate €187 with nothing to show; "Bowl #1" and "Bowl #2" have sky-high CTR (266–302%) but zero results, pointing to a post-click or targeting mismatch.
• 9 of 17 ads have exactly zero results — the creative bench is bloated and underfunded, spreading budget too thin to learn.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more specific business-occasion angles mirroring Koffiebar / Upgrade Brunch / 4 Momenten — each new variant should name a concrete use-case (terrace menu, healthy lunch add-on, takeaway açai).
• Lean into the speed/simplicity story: the "Snel" angle at €12.78 CPR deserves a full creative suite (video prep demos, step-by-step carousels) to validate at scale.
• Introduce video format across winning B2B angles — the entire set is static, leaving the highest-engagement format completely untested.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Both "Boost" variants immediately — vague motivational copy is not what food-service operators respond to.
• "Nutri A #2" — nearly €200 spent, zero results, no signal worth saving.
• Stop spreading €1–€17 across 7+ ads with no learnings; consolidate budget behind 4–5 proven angles to get statistical significance.

Other

13 ads · €291 spend · 1 purchases
✅ What's Working
• "New deliveries! Bekijk ons gamma..." is the only purchase-driving ad at 11.01x ROAS — new-arrivals messaging with Dutch copy converts.
• High engagement rates across the board suggest the audience is warm and interested, but almost nothing converts — the problem is creative/funnel, not reach.
• Product-forward "new delivery" framing clearly outperforms vague or empty posts.
❌ What's Not Working
• Boosted Instagram posts with zero copy (three "Bericht: ''" ads totaling €42 spend, 0 purchases) are pure waste — no hook, no CTA, no conversion intent.
• "Instagram Post" at €80 is the highest spender with zero purchases — generic naming suggests a lazy boost with no conversion objective.
• The opening announcement ("KLAAR VOOR DE OPENING OP 15...") spent €32 with nothing — event-style posts don't drive e-commerce conversions.
⬆ Double Down On
• New arrivals / fresh stock creative with clear product shots, Dutch copy, and a direct shop CTA — replicate the only winning formula.
• Proper conversion-optimized campaigns instead of boosted posts — nearly every ad here looks like a boosted IG post, which Meta optimizes for engagement, not purchases.
• Carousel or collection ads showcasing multiple products with prices visible — give the warm engaged audience a reason to click AND buy.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop boosting posts with empty or emoji-only copy — it burns budget on vanity engagement.
• Stop running ads without a conversion objective — engagement CTRs of 400%+ with zero sales means Meta is finding likers, not buyers.
• Stop spreading €292/month across 13 ads — consolidate into 3-4 properly built conversion campaigns.

🇧🇪

Belgium

2 ads · €90 spend · 0 results
✅ What's Working
• CTRs above 100% on both ads suggest high curiosity and engagement — people are clicking, possibly multiple times per impression.
• The category (workwear/bedrijfskleding) clearly resonates in Belgium; there is demand-side interest worth capturing.
❌ What's Not Working
• Zero results across both ads despite €90 total spend — clicks are not converting, pointing to a broken post-click funnel (landing page, offer, or conversion event misconfiguration).
• 120239393986810631 burned €86 with nothing to show — classic leaky-bucket scenario where ad interest dies at the landing page.
• 120239394435940631 has negligible spend (€4) but mirrors the same zero-conversion pattern, suggesting a systemic funnel issue, not a creative one.
⬆ Double Down On
• Fix the conversion funnel first — audit pixel firing, landing page load speed, and CTA clarity before spending another euro on creative.
• Lean into the high-engagement signal: people want to click on workwear content in this market. Build conversion-optimized creative around that pull.
• Develop Dutch-language, Belgium-specific social proof (local businesses in branded workwear) to bridge the trust gap between click and conversion.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop running traffic to the current landing page/funnel — it is converting at 0% and every euro spent is waste.
• Stop evaluating creative performance until the conversion tracking and post-click experience are verified and functional.

Other

8 ads · €5415 spend · 291 results
✅ What's Working
• 'Calculator' hook is the undisputed champion — Plat dak Calculator delivers 108 leads at €13.07 CPR, nearly half the cost of any Hellend dak variant. Interactive value-first offers crush it.
• Plat dak segment outperforms Hellend dak across the board: 2x cheaper leads and higher engagement. The audience is more price-sensitive and action-ready.
• Vacature Adviseur Plat Dak is a recruitment gem at €3.84/result with 44 results — proves Tectura's employer brand resonates when the role is specific and niche-targeted.
❌ What's Not Working
• Hellend dak leads are consistently expensive (€27-31 CPR) regardless of hook — Calculator, Asbestvrij, and Renovatiekost all cluster around the same high cost. The segment needs a creative breakthrough, not just hook rotation.
• Two plat dak campaigns ('[LEADS] Plat dak | BROAD | Kostprijs 2026' and 'Gratis dakinspectie') have been left to die with €0-1 spend — either they were DOA or never properly launched. Wasted learning opportunity.
• 'Vacature Adviseur Daken' at €14.79 CPR is nearly 4x worse than 'Vacature Adviseur Plat Dak' — generic role naming kills recruitment efficiency.
⬆ Double Down On
• Build more Calculator-style interactive lead magnets for every roof type and scenario — this is your lowest-friction entry point and proven winner.
• Go harder on Plat dak — it's your cheapest lead source by far. Test new angles (subsidies, energy savings, seasonal urgency) all within this segment.
• Specialize recruitment ads by exact role/niche like 'Vacature Adviseur Plat Dak' — specificity drives 4x better results than generic titles.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop rotating Hellend dak hooks without changing the creative format — three hooks, same ~€28 CPR. The problem isn't the message, it's the creative execution.
• Kill the neglect of '[LEADS] Plat dak | BROAD | Kostprijs 2026' and 'Gratis dakinspectie' — either fund them properly for a fair test or archive them. Zombie campaigns waste account structure.

• Double down on social-proof hooks: reviews, client names, before/after results — every ad under €65/result uses this approach.

Other

30 ads · €8302 spend · 136 results
✅ What's Working
• Vottem project dominates: "Vottem_video" (€21.74 CPR, 30 results) and "Vottem_animatie" (€22.98 CPR, 11 results) prove video/animation formats crush static for real estate leads.
• "Brugge_penthouse" delivers strong volume (21 results) at efficient €33.71 CPR — penthouse/premium residential positioning resonates.
• Remarketing rescues failing creatives: "georges_image_cta_v1_rem" (€28.82 CPR, 8 results) turned around the original "georges_image_CTA_v1" which burned €287 for zero results.
❌ What's Not Working
• Wildebeek is a money pit: 4 ads, €1,528 combined spend, only 2 total results. "Flexible units" and "bedrijfsruimte" commercial messaging generates zero interest — the entire project positioning is broken.
• Static image-only launches fail hard: "georges_image_CTA_v1" (€287, 0 results) and "ODD Awans 18/8" (€156, 0 results despite 180% CTR) generate clicks but zero conversions.
• Stokerie ads bleed at scale: "stokerie_terras" ate €698 for only 8 results (€87 CPR), and its remarketing variant "stokerie_terras_rem" is even worse at €149 CPR.
⬆ Double Down On
• Video and animation formats for every project launch — Vottem proves motion creative delivers 2-3x better CPR than static across the board.
• Premium residential positioning with specific unit types (penthouse, terras) outperforms generic commercial/flexible-unit messaging — lean into aspirational property storytelling.
• Remarketing layers on every project showing initial traction — the Georges _rem turnaround (€28.82 vs €0-result original) is a repeatable playbook for Brugge, Vottem, and Charleroi.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all Wildebeek ads immediately — €1,528 for 2 results is indefensible. Reposition the entire project or stop spending.
• Kill static-only project launches — no more image-CTA-only campaigns without a video/animation variant running alongside.
• Kill "Charleroi_te-huur" rental positioning (€139 CPR) — the rental angle isn't converting; "Charleroi_native" at €45 CPR proves the market wants a different format and message.

Belgium

30 ads · €3298 spend · 165 results
✅ What's Working
• "Static _ Doorstromer #1 - Copy" is the undeniable hero: 103 results at €7.24 — massively outperforming every other ad in the account by 10x+ on volume.
• The "- Copy" variant pattern is real: both Doorstromer #1 - Copy (€7.24) and Doorstromer #2 - Copy (€15.22) and Algemeen #2 - Copy (€8.41) crush their originals, suggesting the copy/messaging iteration dramatically improves conversion.
• Doorstromer and Alleenstaand audiences are the only segments producing meaningful results at viable CPAs — one version of Alleenstaand #1 delivers 13 results at €11.24.
❌ What's Not Working
• Original ad versions are burning cash: "Static _ Doorstromer #1" spent €572 for just 3 results (€190.75 CPR) while its Copy variant gets results at €7.24 — that's a 26x efficiency gap on the same creative concept.
• Jong Koppel segment is dead on arrival: three instances of Jong Koppel #1 spent a combined €179 for only 2 results, and Jong Koppel #2 delivered zero. This audience isn't converting.
• Algemeen (general targeting) at higher budgets fails consistently — €212 and €52 spend versions produced 2 and 0 results respectively. Broad targeting is wasting money.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more "- Copy" style messaging iterations of every winning creative. The copy variant treatment is the single biggest lever in this account — apply it systematically to Alleenstaand and any new concepts.
• Invest heavily in Doorstromer-targeted creatives: this audience converts at 5-10x the efficiency of other segments. Build out a full creative suite (video, carousel, UGC) for this persona.
• Scale the Alleenstaand #1 variant that hit €11.24 CPR with 13 results — it's the second-best performer and has room to run with more budget and creative variations.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all Jong Koppel ads immediately. €179 combined spend, 2 total results, no signal worth chasing. Reallocate 100% of that budget to Doorstromer.
• Pause every original ad where a "- Copy" variant exists and outperforms it — specifically "Static _ Doorstromer #1" (€190.75 CPR) and "Static _ Doorstromer #2" (€87.47 CPR). They're cannibalizing budget from their winning counterparts.
• Stop running Algemeen ads at meaningful budgets until you have a creative that proves itself at low spend first. €212 for 2 results is unacceptable.

✅ What's Working

⬆ Double Down On
• PVC veranda-specific creative with the 2026 pricing lock angle — "PVC. VER.- PUB CONVERTION - 2026" proves the niche + urgency combo works at 7x lower cost/result.
• Product-specific segmentation: separate pergola, veranda, and PVC lines into distinct campaigns with tailored creative rather than generic catch-all ads.
• Before/after transformation content — the high CTRs show visual appetite exists; feed it with project showcase reels and carousels that also drive conversion.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop running the generic "VERANDAS - PUB CONVERTIONS" ad — no product specificity, no urgency hook, zero results.
• Stop scaling "PERGOLAS - PUB CONVERTIONS - 2026" at current cost/result without proper ROAS tracking — you're spending €286 with no idea if it's profitable.

Other

30 ads · €7877 spend · 268 results
✅ What's Working
• Carousel format on pergolas is the volume engine — "PERGOLA_CARROUSEL_MUTLI4" drove 100 results at €22.81 CPR, best scale candidate in the account.
• Video format crushes static across categories — "VERANDA VERANCOBEL - VIDEO" (€22.26 CPR, 267% CTR) and "PVCS_VIDEO_MUTLI3" (€19.35 CPR) dramatically outperform their static counterparts.
• Conversion-optimized veranda copy works — "VERANDAS - PUB CONVERTIONS - Copie" at €21.84 CPR is the most efficient veranda ad with real volume behind it.
❌ What's Not Working
• "PERGOLA_CARROUSEL_RJF7" is a €767 black hole — 9 results at €85.17 CPR, nearly 4x worse than the MUTLI4 variant on the same product. Kill it yesterday.
• PVC static ads are wasteful — "PUB PVC 3" (€61.29 CPR) and "PVC VERANCOBEL" at €180 spend (€60.16 CPR) burn budget while the video variant proves the product can convert cheaply.
• "MAQUETTE PERGOLAS" (€63.51 CPR) and "PERGOLA VIDEO_RJF6" (€31 spent, 0 results) are dead weight with no path to efficiency.
⬆ Double Down On
• Video-first creative across ALL product lines — video already wins for verandas and PVC; pergola and carport video is undertested. Produce 3-4 new video ads immediately.
• Carousel format for carports and verandas — carousel drives pergola volume; replicate the MUTLI4 structure for other product categories.
• Conversion-copy approach from verandas applied to pergolas and carports — the "PUB CONVERTIONS" naming suggests a harder CTA/conversion-focused angle that's working at €21.84 CPR.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill "PERGOLA_CARROUSEL_RJF7" — €767 spent at €85 CPR when the same product converts at €22 in another ad. Indefensible.
• Kill all static PVC ads — "PUB PVC 3" and the €180-spend "PVC VERANCOBEL" are 3x the cost of the video PVC variant. Redirect budget to video.
• Kill "MAQUETTE PERGOLAS" and "PERGOLA VIDEO_RJF6" — zero traction, zero reason to continue.

• Hannes - Duinpanne shows some promise among creator ads with 3 results and the highest CTR (52.16%) in that cohort, suggesting this creator/location combo resonates more than others.
• High CTR across the board (30%+) indicates the creative hooks attention — the conversion gap is the problem, not awareness.
❌ What's Not Working
• Creator x location ads are burning budget with near-zero results — Chloe - Bulskampveld spent €214 for literally 0 results, TheLifePlanFamily - Palingbeek spent €228 for 1 result at €228 each.
• Magnolia appears in two ads (Raversyde and Phof) and delivers poorly in both — 2 results combined across €311 spend. This creator partnership is not converting.
• The GIF format (Algemeen - GIF) was barely tested at €1 — a missed opportunity given the static Visual version is the top performer.
⬆ Double Down On
• General/non-creator visuals that sell the province broadly rather than one specific domain — the Algemeen format is 4-13x more efficient than any creator ad.
• Duinpanne as a priority destination — it pulled the best creator-ad results, suggesting this location has the strongest audience appeal.
• Short, punchy formats (GIF/motion graphic) using the Algemeen creative framework — the Visual already proves the concept, now test motion variants.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop running Magnolia as a creator — two ads, two failures, €311 wasted with a blended cost/result over €155.
• Pause Chloe - Bulskampveld immediately — €214 spent, zero results, lowest CTR in the set. Both the creator and the location are underperforming.
• Stop the strategy of pairing one creator with one niche location until you fix the general funnel — the specificity is killing reach and relevance.

Other

11 ads · €783 spend · 15 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Product-named Reels convert: 'Post
• Reel Merlene' is the clear winner at 10.33x ROAS and €8.16 CPP from only €33 spend — proving short-form product Reels drive purchases.
• 'Post
• Reel Mary-Lynn' is the only other ad generating purchases (11), showing the Reel-with-name format has repeatable conversion signal even if this one isn't yet profitable.
• Reel formats dominate engagement and are the only format converting — every static 'Bericht' and event post generated zero purchases.
❌ What's Not Working
• Store/event announcements are pure waste: 'Evenement: Fête des Belges', both 'Deze week kan je hier terecht!' ads, and 'Vanaf nu in onze winkels!' collectively spent €203 with zero purchases — these are awareness posts miscast as conversion ads.
• Sale messaging fails to convert: 'Onze SOLDEN gaan door!', 'De solden zijn gestart!', and 'The Summer Sale just got even...' spent €147 combined with zero purchases — urgency without product focus doesn't work here.
• 'Post
• Reel Mary-Lynn' has highest spend (€351) but ROAS 0.88x — it converts but loses money on every euro, likely a targeting or AOV problem.
⬆ Double Down On
• Product-specific Reels named after the item/collection (Merlene model): shoot 5-10 more in the same style, short-form, product-hero, named clearly. This is the only proven purchase driver.
• Low-CPP acquisition: Merlene's €8.16 CPP suggests a winning creative formula — replicate the exact hook, pacing, and CTA structure across new product lines.
• Dutch-language product Reels with clear e-commerce intent (price, shop-now CTA) instead of vague store/sale announcements that leak budget.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all static 'Bericht' store-visit and event posts running on purchase objectives — they are not conversion creative and have burned €203+ with nothing to show.
• Kill sale/solden announcement posts immediately — €147 wasted; if you run sales, put the discount ON the product Reel, not in a text post.
• Stop scaling Mary-Lynn until ROAS is fixed — €351 at sub-1x is the biggest single budget drain in this account.
